prompt:
I need the front end for Wardway Lobby Guide. The wayfinding system on the touch kiosks in the entrances of a large teaching hospital campus, used by patients, visitors and the volunteers at the information desk to find departments, rooms and the best route there.

Who's using it: Right now it's two people together at the Main Entrance kiosk: Mr. Harold Pettis, 78, arriving with a walker for his first cardiac rehab session, and Gloria, a retired nurse who volunteers at the information desk on Monday mornings and steps over to help when visitors look lost. Harold reads English well but slowly. Gloria knows the campus but not this month's construction detours.

What they're doing right now: Harold's appointment letter says 'Cardiac Rehabilitation, Heart & Vascular Pavilion, Level 2, 10:30 am.' It's 10:12. Elevator bank B in the Pavilion is out of service for maintenance this week, and the second-floor skybridge from the Main Building is closed for construction. Gloria needs to find the department, confirm a step-free route that avoids both closures, see how long the walk takes at a slow pace, and send the directions to Harold's phone or print them, so he can make it on his own while she goes back to the desk.

What's in the system at this point: Campus of 4 connected buildings (Main Building, Heart & Vascular Pavilion, Women's & Children's, Outpatient Center) plus Parking Garage P1 with 5 levels. 212 destinations, each with building, level, room range, phone extension, opening hours and other names people use for it (e.g., 'Cardiac Rehab' = 'Heart Rehab' = 'Cardiopulmonary Rehabilitation'). Route network: corridors, 9 elevator banks, 3 skybridges, stairs, each segment with distance in meters and whether it's step-free. Current closures: Pavilion elevator bank B (Nov 14–20), Level 2 skybridge from Main (until Dec 3), Outpatient Center east doors. Walking times at standard and slow pace (the slow route to Cardiac Rehab is about 9 minutes). Amenities: restrooms, cafeteria, pharmacy, wheelchair loan stations, chapel. Directions available in English, Spanish, Vietnamese and Tagalog.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
